text: Every table already has a built-in REST endpoint, but sometimes that's not enough — you need a custom lookup or a payload shaped exactly how an external system expects it. That's what a Scripted REST API gives you: an endpoint you define yourself, with your own path, method, and script.

Two record types work together. Sys_ws_definition is the API itself — a name and a shared base path, something like slash api slash x underscore acme underscore fleet slash vehicle. A Resource is a child record under that API — one actual endpoint, with its own relative path, its own HTTP method, and its own script. One API can hold several Resources: a GET for reading, a POST for creating, each under that same base path.

Inside a Resource's script, two objects are just handed to you. Request is the incoming call — request dot body dot data holds the parsed JSON body, request dot path params holds any placeholder segments from the URL, and request dot query params holds question-mark key-value pairs. Response is how you answer back — response dot set body serializes a JavaScript object as JSON, and response dot set status sets the HTTP status code.

Here's a real GET resource at the path slash incident slash curly-brace number. ServiceNow parses that placeholder automatically into request dot path params dot number. From there it's the exact same GlideRecord query pattern you've used all course — query the incident table by number, and if nothing comes back, set status 404 and send an error body. If a record is found, build a plain object with the fields you want and hand it to response dot set body.

This lesson stays at the fundamentals level on purpose. Authentication schemes, versioning an API across releases, custom headers, and making outbound REST calls from ServiceNow to other systems are real, important topics — they belong to the next course in this path, ServiceNow IntegrationHub and REST APIs. For now, the model to hold onto is simple: a Resource is a URL plus a method plus a script, request in, response out.

A Resource's path and method, request in, response out — that's the whole shape of a Scripted REST endpoint. Next up: Script Actions and Scheduled Scripts, two more ways server-side script code runs without a user sitting in front of a form.
